changes.text: 救兵被自己的国君叫停在半路，一个手里没有兵的公子还能做什么？
When your own king halts the relief army halfway, what can a prince with no troops do?
魏公子无忌带着百余乘车骑出了大梁城，准备去秦军阵前拼命，与赵国同归于尽。车过城东的夷门，他停下来见守门的老人侯嬴，把这打算原原本本告诉了他。侯嬴只送了一句「公子勉之矣，老臣不能從」。车队走出几里，《史记》写无忌「心不快」；他掉转车头，回来问侯嬴。

Prince Wuji rode out of the city of Daliang with a hundred-odd chariots and horsemen, intending to hurl himself at the Qin army and die alongside the state of Zhao. Passing the Yimen, the eastern gate of the city, he stopped to see Hou Ying, the aged gatekeeper there, and told him the plan outright. Hou Ying saw him off with a single line — "Push on, my lord; I am old and cannot follow you". The column had gone a few li when the Records of the Grand Historian has Wuji "troubled in his heart"; he turned the chariots around and came back to ask Hou Ying what he had missed.
平原君的使者一批接一批赶到魏国，冠盖相属，责备公子说：我高攀这门婚姻，是以为公子高义、能急人之困；如今邯郸旦暮降秦而魏国救兵不至，这份高义在哪里？哪怕你看不起我，独不怜公子姊邪——难道连你的姐姐也不可怜吗？

Lord Pingyuan's envoys now arrived in Wei in an unbroken stream, official carriages crowding the road, and reproached the prince in their master's name: I attached myself to this marriage because I took the prince for a man of high principle, one who hurries to relieve another's distress. Now Handan may surrender to Qin any day and Wei's rescue has not come — where is that principle? "Even if you think little of me, have you no pity for your own sister?"

魏国有位隐士侯嬴，年七十，家贫，在大梁夷门守门。无忌想厚赠他，他不肯收，说自己修身絜行几十年，终不能因为守门穷困而受财。无忌于是置酒大会宾客，空出车上左边的尊位，亲自去迎侯嬴。侯嬴穿着破旧衣冠，径直登上上座，也不谦让，为的是看无忌的反应；无忌执辔，愈恭。侯嬴又让车骑停在集市里，去拜访一位朋友，久久站着，借此观察无忌；无忌的脸色始终不变。到家后无忌请他坐上座，向在座宾客一一介绍，宾客皆惊。侯嬴后来自己说破：他这样做是想成全公子礼贤下士的名声；市人因此把他看作小人，称无忌是能下士的长者。宴罢，侯嬴成为上客。

Wei had a recluse named Hou Ying, seventy years old and poor, a gatekeeper at the Yimen. Wuji sought him out and tried to present him with a handsome gift. Hou Ying would not take it: he had kept himself and his conduct clean for decades, he said, and would not accept the prince's money simply because gatekeeping left him poor. So Wuji laid on a feast for all his retainers, and once the guests were seated, he went out with his carriage and escort, left the seat of honor on the left of the chariot empty, and fetched Hou Ying himself. Hou Ying, in his shabby robe and cap, climbed straight up into that seat without a word of demur — a test of Wuji, this was — and Wuji took the reins and grew only more respectful. Hou Ying then had Wuji's carriage wait in the marketplace while he went to call on a friend, standing there a long time and watching Wuji; Wuji's manner never changed. At the house Wuji showed Hou Ying to the seat of honor and presented him to the assembled guests one by one, and the guests were astonished. Hou Ying later spelled out his reasoning: he was a mere gatekeeper, and the prince had personally come for him before a crowd. He had wanted to make the prince's name, so he kept the prince's carriage standing in the market while he called on a friend and watched the prince, and the prince only grew more respectful. The townsfolk took Hou Ying for a lout and Wuji for a true elder who can humble himself before scholars. When the feast broke up, Hou Ying became one of Wuji's most honored guests.

无忌折回夷门，侯嬴对他说，带门客去冲秦军，就像拿肉投给饿虎，毫无用处；公子待他厚，公子走而他不送，他由此知道公子会心怀不满而折回。接着侯嬴献上一个计策。晋鄙的兵符平时收在魏王卧室内；如姬最得魏王宠爱，出入卧内，有能力偷出来。侯嬴说，如姬的父亲被人所杀，她为此出资三年，从魏王以下都想替她报父仇而未能；如姬向无忌哭诉，无忌派门客斩了仇人的头献给她。侯嬴的判断是：如姬愿为公子死，只是没有机会；公子一开口，她必答应。得虎符，夺晋鄙军，北救赵而西却秦，「此五霸之伐也」。

When Wuji came back to the Yimen, Hou Ying told him that charging the Qin army with his retainers would be like throwing meat to a starving tiger — it would accomplish nothing. The prince had treated him generously, he said, and when the prince left without being seen off, Hou Ying had known the prince would resent it and come back. Then Hou Ying laid out a plan. Jin Pi's command tally was normally kept in the king of Wei's bedchamber. Lady Ru, the king's favorite, came and went in the bedchamber freely and could steal it out. Hou Ying spelled out why she would. Her father had been murdered; for three years she had put up money to see her father's death avenged, and no one, the king included, had been able to bring it off. She had wept to Wuji, who sent a retainer to cut off her enemy's head and present it to her. Hou Ying's judgment was that Lady Ru would gladly die for Wuji and had simply never had the chance to serve him; one word from the prince and she would agree. Get the tally, take over Jin Pi's army, go north to rescue Zhao and push Qin back from the west — "an achievement worthy of the Five Hegemons."

Third, how he kept the books after it worked. Zhao was about to grant five cities; a retainer reminded him that he could not count as a loyal minister to Wei, and he blamed himself on the spot. Before the king of Zhao he declared he had failed Wei and done nothing for Zhao. While he was staying in Zhao he still said he had failed his king to save Zhao. On this reading he did not write the debt off: the army went home to Wei, and he stayed in Zhao. But the record also says he stayed in Zhao ten years without returning; when the king of Wei sent men to fetch him, he feared the king's anger and even barred his household from admitting the king's envoys, so staying there need not count as settling the debt.

dispositions.rationale: 摘要改为问题式，不再预告hook.1中的十万大军止步和百余乘车骑等情节；中英同步。
E9中的年份对应秦围邯郸、魏王派晋鄙出兵，不能确定无忌出城也在这一年。hook.0中英文句首的年份均已删去，年份仍在context.0的证据范围内。
删去读者不认识的“赵胜/Zhao Sheng”，改为“我/me”，避免误以为出现了另一个人。
按E7“過客以觀公子”和E8中“過”的用法，把“让过路人围观”改为侯嬴把车骑停在市中、去拜访朋友，借此观察无忌。英文叙述同步修改，侯嬴自陈部分去掉引号改为转述，并删去“while people watched”，与中文一致。
在story.0开头用白话补上侯嬴折返时的回答：赴秦军如以肉投饿虎、毫无用处，以及他因未送行而料到公子会折回。这样读者能看出无忌为何转而听计。story.0的ev补入E14，中英同步，没有另加对白或场面。
英文首句由定论式的“kept the books honestly”改为中性的“how he kept the books after it worked”，与中文一致，也不与段末的保留意见冲突。
